full_judgment:
This Rule is directed against the order dated 14.3.77 passed by the Special Judge, Khulna Division in Special Case No. 53-C/ 1969 assuming jurisdiction under Criminal Law (Amendment) Act, 1958 to try the accused petitioners and rejecting application challenging the jurisdiction of the Special Judge. Facts leading to this Rule are as follows: 

 4. On 14.3.71 the accused petitioner filed a petition before the Special Judge claiming to be servants of Khulna Newsprint Mills Ltd. and not public servants as defined in section 21 of the Penal Code and as such they contended that they were not liable to be tried for the alleged offences by Special Judge under Criminal Law (Amendment) Act, 1958. Petitioners alleged that they being employees of a public limited company, namely. Khulna Newsprint Mills Ltd. were not public servant within meaning of Act II of 1947 or under Criminal Law Amendment Act on the date the alleged offences were said to have been committed and that the learned Special Judge has no jurisdiction to try the petitioners. The learned Special Judge rejected the petition holding that the question of jurisdiction could not be decided without taking evidence, and he proceeded with the trial. 

 6. He has further submitted that the form of trial will be determined by the law that existed on the date of alleged commission of the offence. It has also been urged by the learned Advocate for the petitioners that having regard to the variation in punishment provided for in the Special Laws, namely, Prevention of Corruption Act and Criminal Law (Amendment) Act, of 1958, which are sought to be applied, retrospective effect can not be given to the amendment of these laws to give jurisdiction to the Special Judge to try the accused petitioners. He has also submitted that even if the amended laws would be applicable to the employees of a public limited company, the accused petitioners being not public servants at the relevant time, the Special Judge has no jurisdiction to try the accused petitioners. 

 7. It is evident from the charge-sheet and from the records of this case that the accused petitioners were employees of Khulna Newsprint Mills Ltd. The allegation in the charge-sheet, inter alia, were that the petitioner No. 2 in the capacity of Cashier of Khulna Newsprint Mills Ltd. misappropriated a sum of Rs. 10,000/- between 5.11.64 and 16.11.64 by making short deposits in the bank and tampering with the official records and books of accounts of the company and that the petitioner Nos. 1 and 3 in the capacity of Financial Accountant and Office Manager respectively of the Khulna Newsprint Mills Ltd. abetted the commission of the said offence and a charge-sheet was submitted against them. It is seen that charge-sheet under section 409 Penal Code and under section 5(2) of Act II of 1947 was submitted against the petitioner No. 2, and under section 409/109 B.P.C. and under section 5(2) of Act II of 1947 against petitioner Nos. 2 and 3 and, as had been stated above, the accused petitioners were placed on trial before the learned Special Judge, Khulna Division, under Criminal Law (Amendment) Act, 1958. The offence were alleged to have been committed by the accused petitioners between 5,11.64. and 16.11.64. Prevention of Corruption Act was amended by Anti-Corruption Laws Amendments Act, 1965 on 31.7.65. The amendment runs as follows:— 

 "In section 2 after the words "Penal Code" the words "and includes an employee of any corporation or other body, or organisation set up by Central Government" were added. 

 9. It is seen that if these amended laws are applied retrospectively the accused petitioners could be called public servants. Let me consider first whether these laws are procedural in nature or substantive laws. If these laws are procedural in nature then these will apply retrospectively. Amendment of law on a Matter of procedure applies retrospectively. It has been submitted by the learned Advocate for the petitioners that these amended laws are not procedure in nature since these laws have affected and changed the status of the accused petitioners from ordinary citizen to that of public servant. Secondly, he submitted that by application of these amended laws a different kind of punishment has been provided for the persons guilty under section 409 P.C. in as much as that with sentence of imprisonment and fine under section 409 of 'Penal Code, compulsory imposition of fine to the extent of the gain the accused persons were alleged to have made by misappropriation had also to be inflicted upon by treating the accused persons as public servants under the amended enactments. The learned Advocate for the petitioners has also submitted that in the absence of any clear intention in the amended enactments to give retrospective operation those laws are presumed to be applicable prospectively. I am of the view that the aforesaid amending enactments were not given retrospective operation and hence on the date when the offences were alleged to have been committed by accused petitioners they were not public servants and as such the learned Special Judge had no jurisdiction to try them under Pakistan Criminal Law (Amendment) Act, 1958. I am also of the view that a law changing the character of an accused person from an ordinary citizen to that of a public servant and providing a variation of punishment of an accused person to his prejudice cannot be said to be a procedural law. It is true that it is not always easy to make a distinction between substantiate and procedural law but generally it can be said that law' which governs the principles of litigation is a procedural law and the rest are substantive law. A law which aggravates a crime or its punishment or changes the punishments by changing the character of the accused persons cannot be said to be a procedural law. In this connection I may refer to the decision in the case of Nabi Ahmed V. Home Secretary, Govt. of West Pakistan in (1970) 22 DLR. (SC) 20; P.L.D. 1969 (S.C.) 599 In that decision their Lordships while dealing with ex post facto legislation observed as follows: 

 Mr. Serajul Huque, the learned Advocate on behalf on the accused petitioners has also referred to a decision reported in the case of A.K.M.A. Alim V. The State in 29 D.L.R. page 218 in which his Lordship considered an identical case where an accountant of Khulna Newsprint Mills Ltd. was an accused and held that the accused would not be a public servant in 1962 when the alleged offences of criminal breach of trust were alleged to have been committed by him by reason of amendment of Anti-Corruption Act and Criminal Law (Amendment) Act, 1958. Mr. Serajul Haque also referred to me a decision reported in the case of Al-Haj Abdul. Rob V. The State reported in 20 D.L.R. (Dacca) page 876 (para 16). Referring to this decision he has submitted that even if the amendments of Criminal Law (Amendment) Act 1958 by Criminal Law (Amendment) (East Pakistan Amendment) Act of 1957 is applicable yet an employee of Public Ltd. Company cannot be said to be a public servant by virtue of the amendment. In the aforesaid case, the accused was the Managing Director of a Jute Mills and he claimed to be a public servant on the basis of Criminal Law (Amendment) Act (East Pakistan Amendment) 1967, and submitted that the learned Magistrate had no jurisdiction to enquire and hold committal proceedings. The observations in this connection made by their Lordships in the aforesaid are as follows:— 

 "14. By referring to Pakistan Criminal Law Amendment (East Pakistan Amendment) Act III of 1967), the learned Advocate has lastly contended that the accused being the Managing Director of the Delta Jute Mills is a public servant and the learned Magistrate has no jurisdiction to enquire and hold the committal proceeding and the alleged offence being exclusively triable by the Special Judge appointed under Criminal Law Amendment Act, 1958, commitment is bad in law." This contention, in our opinion, is based on misconception. Section 3 of the Pakistan Criminal Law Amendment (East Pakistan Amendment) Act, 1967 on which the learned Advocate relies reads as follows: 

 (i)	clause (a), for the words and comma "by an organisation or body corporate notified by the central Govt. in pursuance of the next succeeding clause" the words and comma "by a corporation or other body or organisation set up by the central Government", shall be substituted; and 

 11. I have already found that these amended enactments are not applicable retrospectively to include the accused petitioners as public servants as defined in section 21 of the Penal Code, and, as such, I hold that the learned Special Judge had no jurisdiction to try the accused petitioners under Pakistan Criminal Law (Amendment) Act, 1958. The accused petitioners are, however, liable to be tried for the alleged offences by ordinary Criminal Court under Code of Criminal Procedure.
